title: The Multi-organ Chip - A Microfluidic Platform for Long-term Multi-tissue Coculture
protocol: Remove the medium from confluent, differentiated monolayer cultures of HepaRG cells grown in cell culture flasks (75 cm²).
Wash HepaRG cells with PBS twice.
Add 3 ml of 0.05% Trypsin/EDTA to the cells and incubate for 3 to 5 min at 37°C.
Stop the trypsin reaction by adding 6 ml of trypsin inhibitor.
Centrifuge HepaRG cells at 150 x g for 5 min, then remove supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 ml of HepaRG cell culture medium and count cells.
Remove the medium from monolayer cultures of HHSteC cells.
Wash HHSteC cells with PBS twice.
Add 3 ml of 0.05% Trypsin/EDTA to the cells and incubate for 5 min at 37°C.
Stop the trypsin reaction by adding 6 ml of trypsin inhibitor.
Centrifuge HHSteC cells at 150 x g for 5 min, then remove supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 ml of HepaRG cell culture medium and count cells.
Combine HepaRG and HHSteC cells at a ratio of 24:1 in HepaRG cell culture medium.
Dilute the cell suspensions as necessary to achieve a concentration of 4.8 x 10^6 cells/ml for HepaRG and 1 x 10^5 cells/ml for HHSteC.
Mix the combined cell suspension carefully.
Add 2 ml of PBS to the hanging drop plate and receiver plate.
Pipette 20 μl of the mixed cell suspension into each well of the hanging drop plate.
Place the plate in a 37 °C incubator.
Wait 48 hours for spheroids to form.
Cut pipette tips or widen them with a sterile knife to about 2-3 mm.
Use wide-tipped pipettes to handle and retrieve spheroids without disrupting them.
Wash off spheroids carefully from the hanging drop plate by repeatedly adding 1 ml of media using a pipette.
Collect spheroids in the receiver plate.
Transfer up to 20 spheroids per well to 24-well ultra-low attachment plates using prepared pipette tips.
Adjust media volume in each well to 0.5 ml.
Inoculate one MOC circuit with 20 aggregates for a miniaturization rate of 1/100,000 regarding in vivo cell numbers.
Incubate spheroids at 37 °C and 5% CO2 until further use in the MOC.
Do not store spheroids longer than three days before usage to assure comparability.
Cultivate aggregates for at least one day in ultra-low attachment plates to retrieve homogenous spheroids.
Cut transwells with an incandescent knife below the bracket to prepare 96-well cell culture inserts.
Store prepared transwell inserts under sterile conditions until further use.
Sterilize prepuce samples in 80% ethanol for 30 seconds and cut the ring open.
Ensure samples have an average height of 2 mm.
Cut biopsies of 4.5 mm diameter using a biopsy punch to obtain an equal miniaturization ratio for both liver and skin.
Load biopsies into prepared 96-well transwell inserts with forceps.
Position biopsies with the epidermal side facing upwards.
Place cell culture inserts with biopsies in a receiver plate containing HepaRG cell culture medium.
Store the plate at 37 °C and 5% CO2 until further use in the MOC.
Do not store samples longer than 2 to 3 hours.
Integrate ready-made in vitro skin models into the MOC, ensuring they are in 96-well transwell format.
Use the cell culture medium supplied by the vendor or a minimal medium supporting both tissues if coculture is envisaged.
Test the respective minimal medium in prior static experiments for its capacity to support the tissues.
Retrieve skin models from the holder plate and cut the 96-well inserts below the bracket with an incandescent knife.
Place the inserts back into the receiver plate and store at 37 °C and 5% CO2 until further use in the MOC.
Do not store samples longer than one day.
Mix PDMS and curing agent at a ratio of 10:1 (v/v).
Place the mixture under vacuum for 15 min to remove air bubbles.
Meanwhile, treat a polycarbonate cover-plate with the silicon rubber additive at 80 °C for 20 min.
Insert Teflon screws into respective holes of the cover-plate to create the four PDMS-free cell culture compartments and the six PDMS membranes.
Plug the prepared cover-plate to the master mold of the two microvascular circuits.
Inject degassed PDMS into the system carefully.
Remove air bubbles by tilting the device if they emerge.
Incubate the system at 80 °C for 60 min to cure the PDMS layer.
Remove the master mold and Teflon screws from the device.
Bond the PDMS layer to a glass slide with low pressure plasma oxidation.
Screw special thread MOC adapters to all four cell culture compartments of the cover-plate.
Connect syringes containing culture medium to female Luer x ¼-28 male adapters.
Screw the connected syringes to the MOC adapters on the cover-plate.
Inject the medium into the microfluidic circuit by repeatedly pushing down and pulling up the syringe plungers.
Check the proper filling of the channels with medium under a microscope.
Flush each MOC circuit with endothelial cell growth medium.
Incubate the flushed circuits statically for three days at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Sterilize the MOCs using an ethanol wipe.
Place the sterilized MOCs under a laminar flow bench.
Sterilize two pairs of forceps and two hexagonal keys.
Loosen the caps of the tissue culture compartment of the MOC using hexagonal keys.
Remove the caps using forceps.
Insert the medium into the compartments.
Screw the caps back onto the MOCs.
Remove the medium from HDMEC monolayer cultures.
Wash the cells with PBS twice.
Add 3 ml of 0.05% Trypsin/EDTA to the cells.
Incubate for 5 min at 37 °C.
Stop the reaction by adding 6 ml of trypsin inhibitor.
Centrifuge the HDMEC at 220 x g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 ml of endothelial cell growth medium.
Count cells; ensure viability is >90%.
Adjust the cell count to a final concentration of 2 x 10^7 cells/ml using endothelial cell growth medium.
Transfer 250 μl of the adjusted cell suspension into a 1 ml syringe.
Apply the cell solution to the MOC at a miniaturization rate of 1/100,000 for all organs.
Connect an empty syringe in the same way to the second compartment of the MOC circuit.
Inject cells evenly by pushing down and pulling up the two syringe plungers several times consecutively.
Control cell infusion under the microscope.
Incubate the MOC at 37 °C and 5% CO2 under static conditions for 3 hr to allow cell adherence.
Remove the chip from the incubator and place it under a laminar flow bench.
Replace the syringes and the MOC adapters with special thread MOC cell culture chambers.
Add 400 µl of fresh medium to one compartment of each MOC circuit.
Let the medium flush through the channels by hydrostatic pressure.
Replace the medium in both compartments with 300 µl of fresh medium.
Close the compartments using caps, as described.
Connect the chip to the pump control unit.
Adjust the pumping velocity to a frequency of 0.475 Hz.
Cultivate the chip at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Replace the medium of each MOC compartment every one to two days.
Monitor cell morphology by light microscopy.
Place the MOC under the laminar flow bench.
Open it, as described in step 3.1.2.
Remove the media from the tissue culture compartments.
Replace it with 300 µl of fresh HepaRG cell culture medium.
Transfer 20 preformed spheroids to one tissue culture compartment of each MOC circuit using pipette tips with a wide opening.
Close the cap using forceps and hexagonal keys.
Transfer 96-well cell culture inserts containing skin equivalents to the remaining tissue culture compartment of each MOC circuit using forceps.
Insert transwells at a slightly tilted angle and push down gently to avoid bubble formation below the membrane.
Remove excess medium around the transwell by pipetting up from below.
Close the cap using forceps and hexagonal keys.
Set operational parameters in the control units to desired values.
Modify air pressure, vacuum, and pumping frequency as needed.
Connect the MOC containing tissue equivalents to the pump control units.
Insert air pressure tubing to the respective fittings on the MOC.
Cultivate the MOC at 37 °C and 5% CO2 in an incubator or use the heated support for live tissue imaging under a microscope.
Perform routine media exchange every day or every other day based on cell type and metabolic activity.
Retrieve the MOC from the incubator.
Observe the MOC under the microscope to control media flow rates and check for contamination.
Disconnect the MOC from the pump control unit by unplugging the air pressure tubing.
Sterilize the MOC using ethanol wipes.
Put the sterilized MOC under the laminar flow bench.
Open the tissue culture compartment containing liver spheroids.
Remove up to 200 µl of medium without disrupting the spheroids and store it in an empty well of a deep-well plate.
Analyze the media sample directly or close the deep-well plate and store samples at -80 °C for further analysis.
Replace the medium with up to 250 µl fresh cell culture medium and close the cap.
Open the tissue culture compartment holding skin equivalents to check for tissue intactness, taking care not to introduce air bubbles into the system.
Close the cap after checking.
Connect the tubing of the pump control unit to the MOC according to step 5.3.
Place the MOC in an incubator.
Analyze tissue culture performance on-line using live cell imaging.
Remove the media from endothelialized MOC as described in steps 6.1.1 to 6.1.4.
Replace the removed media with 200 μl of 10 µg/ml fluorophore conjugated acetylated LDL solution diluted in cell culture media in both compartments.
Close the caps securely.
Connect the MOC to the pump control unit according to step 5.3.
Pump for 30 min at 0.475 Hz to distribute the solution evenly within the microfluidic circuit.
Stop the pumping and incubate the MOC statically for 3.5 hr at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Remove the acetylated LDL solution from both compartments.
Replace the removed solution with 400 μl of fresh medium in one compartment.
Wait for 3 to 5 min to allow hydrostatic pressure to drive the medium through the microfluidic channel circuit.
Replace the medium which has flowed through with 300 μl of fresh medium.
Fill the second tissue culture compartment with 300 μl of fresh medium.
Close the MOC according to step 3.1.2.
Place the closed MOC under a fluorescence microscope to observe cell growth and viability.
Return the stained MOC to the incubator for continued cultivation.
Remove any stain leaking out of the cells with each media replacement.
Retrieve tissue equivalents from the MOC at the end of the experiment for endpoint analyses.
Remove the medium from each tissue culture compartment as described in steps 6.1.1 to 6.1.4.
Use forceps to remove the 96-well cell culture inserts containing skin from the MOC.
Peel off the membrane carefully by gripping it on one side and pulling down, being cautious not to lose the skin equivalent.
Freeze the membrane holding the skin equivalent in cryo-embedding compound and store at -80°C for further analysis.
Remove liver equivalents similarly from the tissue culture compartment using pipette tips.
Embed liver spheroids in cryo-embedding compound carefully, removing any excess liquid with a pipette.
Place the spheroids onto the embedding compound and add more cryo-compound to fully enclose them.
Freeze the liver equivalents and store at -80°C for further analysis.
Cut the tissue equivalents in a cryo-microtome to 8 μm sections for endpoint analysis.
Stain the sections for tissue-specific markers as described in previous protocols.
